# Webb direct-line proof frontier — 1773 Saybrook marriage does NOT identify the groom
Research checkpoint: 2026-10-17; **one direct-line subject: James Webb (born about 21 March 1777; died 17 March 1845), FamilySearch KWJ1-P2V**.
**Research-only; do not edit FamilySearch, approved Atlas biography, parent links or public relationship confidence without a distinguishing original.**

## Existing person and audit facts, NOT new discoveries
- James Webb (KWJ1-P2V) has contemporaneous indexed Nauvoo Neighbor report, **26 March 1845, p.3 col.3**, sexton's March17 death: “James Webb, of Laharp, 67y, 11m, 26d; fever.” The age mathematically matches birth about March21 1777; this individual and his spouse Hannah Griswold/son Edward Milo Sr are separately rooted through later records. Source already in Sept 2026 101-person audit; not newly found.
- The working connection to **James Webb born 1733 (LKKM-KR5)** and **Elizabeth Douglass L89B-86R** is already flagged as an *unproved conflation*, not a proved parent couple. The 1733 man separately had a family with **Elizabeth Welch in Horton, Nova Scotia around 1761**, and early 1766 property trail; old 101 audit already documents this. His 1733 profile itself disputes assigning the Elizabeth Douglass marriage to him.
- A *different* **James Webb born 14 April 1754**, FamilySearch **LHSH-TKQ**, listed as son of **Samuel Webb and Mary Catlin**, has an indexed spouse **Elizabeth Douglas**, and a compiled child set **Stephen Webb b.1777**, Samuel, Curtis, Elizabeth, Polly — **not James Webb b.1777**. His FS page has 4 sources, including 1820 census, "John Webb of Saybrook", *American Genealogist* vol.24 pp171–179, and 1800 census: https://ancestors.familysearch.org/en/LHSH-TKQ/james-webb-1754-1823 . This is useful independent-*candidate identification* but a modern compiled profile, not evidence of the 1773 groom's parentage.

## What is actually recorded and what it DOESN'T prove
- Frederic W. Bailey, editor, **Early Connecticut Marriages as Found on Ancient Church Records Prior to 1800**, Second Book (New Haven, 1896), Saybrook Congregational marriages **printed p.90**, includes the pair **James Webb & Elizabeth Douglas, married 9 December 1773** amid adjacent dated Saybrook marriages. Readable scanned edition/transcription https://godfreydata.org/books/US0267.pdf ; text mirrors https://www.newhorizonsgenealogicalservices.com/connecticut-genealogy/middlesex/saybrook_ct_marriage_records_1800.htm .
- This is a **printed transcription of earlier church entries**, not the actual **1773 manuscript page**. The entry as printed gives **only names and date**, **no ages, parents, occupation, birthplace or identifier**; it alone cannot decide among the 1733 and 1754 same-name men and cannot name the father of our 1777 James. Same-name identical date indexing is a likely source of tree conflation.
- The 1754 man would be **19** at a December 1773 marriage; the 1733 man would be **40**. Ages are arithmetically compatible and NOT proof of groom identity. The older man had a recorded earlier Nova Scotia wife; without death/divorce or period marriage evidence no serial/plural assumption or conclusion. Particularly do not import a Nova Scotia citizenship link via the wrong James.

## Original manuscript / no-cost access target — NEW precisely scoped catalog and custodian
- FamilySearch Library catalogs the **Old Saybrook Congregational Church manuscript records, 1736–1842**, plus **Saybrook, Connecticut, church records, Frederick L’Hommedieu copy**, comprising **Old Saybrook 1736–1782, Centerbrook 1759–1832, Chester 1759–1835**. Record coverage includes the **9 Dec 1773** reported ceremony. Independent catalogue source https://ldsgenealogy.com/CT/Middlesex-County-Church-Records.htm . A catalog entry indicates coverage, NOT an examined original or availability of digital image.
- The **Old Saybrook Historical Society's Frank Stevenson Archives** publicly states it holds some original First Church of Christ records (not necessarily this 1773 page): https://saybrookhistory.org/stevenson-archives-library/ . Actual church official contact: https://firstchurchsaybrook.org/contact ; do NOT send enquiries without user-specific permission. User only authorizes free sources and explicitly prohibits any unrequested email access.
- A 1773 manuscript inspection can authenticate **actual wording**, but if it too gives just names/date, identity still hinges on collateral probate/land/household continuity (birth/baptism of our James c1777, direct parentage, land linking the 1754 or 1733 households). Priority should be 1774–1780 Saybrook baptisms, 1798/1808 Otsego deeds naming father/son and locality, and later contemporary 1845 obituary/lineage IDs, not yet another generic “James Webb” tree.
